title: Android Jetpack Compose Modifiers
description: Beginner-to-advanced reference for modifier order, constraints, layout, drawing, input, focus, semantics, reuse, parent data, and custom Modifier.Node implementations.

sections.title: Modifier Model & API Contract
sections.description: A Modifier is an immutable ordered chain of elements wrapping a layout node.

subtopics.title: Order Changes Behavior
subtopics.description: Each modifier wraps everything after it. Earlier elements are outer wrappers; layout constraints travel inward and size/placement return outward.

tabs.label: Padding Clickable
tabs.code:
Modifier
    .padding(16.dp)
    .clickable(onClick)
    .background(Color.Blue)
// Outer padding is not clickable or blue.

tabs.label: Clickable Padding
tabs.code:
Modifier
    .clickable(onClick)
    .background(Color.Blue)
    .padding(16.dp)
// Click/background include the padded area.

callouts.title: Read Outside In
callouts.text: Reason through a chain from top to bottom as nested wrappers. Ask which wrapper owns hit testing, clipping, drawing, constraints, and semantics.

subtopics.title: Accept and Respect modifier
subtopics.description: Reusable UI elements should accept one optional Modifier parameter, default to Modifier, and apply it to the first emitted UI node.

callouts.title: Do Not Replace the Caller Chain
callouts.text: Apply behavior by extending the received modifier. Starting from Modifier inside the component discards caller size, test tags, semantics, and placement expectations.

subtopics.title: Layout, Draw, Input, Semantics & Parent Data
subtopics.description: Modifier elements participate in different phases. A chain may affect measurement, placement, drawing, pointer/focus input, accessibility, or a specific parent layout.

table.title: Modifier Category Reference
rows: High; changes constraints and bounds seen downstream
High; wraps or transforms later drawing
High; hit area follows its position in the chain
Medium; merge and clear operations can replace descendants
Instructions consumed by a specific parent
Scope-bound; ignored outside the matching parent scope

codeBlocks.code:
Layout: size, padding, offset, aspectRatio, layout
Draw: background, border, clip, alpha, drawBehind
Input: clickable, scrollable, pointerInput, focusable
Semantics: contentDescription, role, stateDescription, testTag
Parent data: weight in Row/Column, align in Box, matchParentSize
Graphics: graphicsLayer, transform, render effects

sections.title: Constraints, Size & Position
sections.description: Use constraints deliberately and distinguish measurement from visual translation.

subtopics.title: size, requiredSize, fill & sizeIn
subtopics.description: size requests a preferred size constrained by the parent; requiredSize can force a child beyond incoming constraints; fill consumes available bounded space; sizeIn sets ranges.

codeBlocks.code:
Modifier
    .fillMaxWidth()
    .heightIn(min = 48.dp, max = 96.dp)

Modifier.size(64.dp)          // respects parent constraints
Modifier.requiredSize(64.dp)  // may violate them; parent masks/centers view of child

callouts.title: Unbounded Axes
callouts.text: fillMaxHeight inside a vertically scrolling/unbounded parent cannot consume infinity. Understand which axis the parent bounds and prefer intrinsic/content sizing when appropriate.

subtopics.title: padding vs offset
subtopics.description: padding changes measurement constraints and reported size; offset changes placement without changing the size reported to the parent.

codeBlocks.code:
Modifier.padding(start = 16.dp) // siblings account for space
Modifier.offset(x = 16.dp)       // visual shift; siblings do not reflow
Modifier.offset { IntOffset(animatedX.roundToInt(), 0) } // defer state read to layout

callouts.title: Logical vs Absolute Direction
callouts.text: offset(x=...) follows layout direction; absoluteOffset does not. Prefer logical start/end behavior for RTL-compatible UI.

subtopics.title: aspectRatio, wrapContent & Intrinsics
subtopics.description: aspectRatio chooses a size satisfying a ratio within constraints; wrapContent changes how minimum constraints and placement are handled; intrinsic measurement should be used sparingly.

codeBlocks.code:
Image(
    painter = painter,
    contentDescription = null,
    modifier = Modifier
        .fillMaxWidth()
        .aspectRatio(16f / 9f)
)

callouts.title: Intrinsic Measurement Costs
callouts.text: Intrinsic queries add a pre-measure pass and some custom layouts do not support meaningful intrinsics. Prefer explicit constraints or a custom single-pass layout when performance matters.

sections.title: Appearance, Clipping & Drawing
sections.description: Control which area is painted, clipped, transformed, and cached.

subtopics.title: background, border & clip Order
subtopics.description: Drawing modifiers paint within the size at their position in the chain. Clip affects subsequent drawing and content.

callouts.title: Visual and Touch Shapes Differ
callouts.text: Clipping changes pixels, but gesture hit testing and semantics may still use rectangular bounds depending on APIs. Verify both visuals and interaction.

subtopics.title: drawBehind, drawWithContent & drawWithCache
subtopics.description: drawBehind paints before content; drawWithContent controls ordering; drawWithCache caches objects until size/state dependencies change.

callouts.title: Cache Expensive Draw Objects
callouts.text: Use drawWithCache when brushes, paths, or other allocations depend on size/state. Do not add caching when the drawing is already trivial.

subtopics.title: graphicsLayer & Transformations
subtopics.description: graphicsLayer can transform drawing without remeasurement and isolate content into a layer when needed.

codeBlocks.code:
Modifier.graphicsLayer {
    alpha = animatedAlpha
    translationX = dragOffset
    rotationZ = rotation
    scaleX = scale
    scaleY = scale
    clip = true
    shape = RoundedCornerShape(16.dp)
}

callouts.title: Layers Have Cost
callouts.text: A graphics layer can improve repeated transformations but consumes rendering resources. Add it for a measured need, not as a universal optimization.

sections.title: Interaction, Gestures, Focus & Scrolling
sections.description: Prefer high-level components and modifiers before raw pointer handling.

subtopics.title: clickable, selectable & toggleable
subtopics.description: Choose a semantic interaction modifier matching the control: action, single selection, or boolean state.

callouts.title: One Interaction Target
callouts.text: Making the row toggleable and the child Switch passive creates one large accessible target without duplicate click actions or semantics.

subtopics.title: pointerInput & Gesture Detectors
subtopics.description: Use pointerInput for custom gestures not covered by clickable, draggable, scrollable, transformable, or nested-scroll APIs.

callouts.title: Keys Restart Gesture Handling
callouts.text: pointerInput cancels and restarts its coroutine when keys change. Include values whose change must alter the handler, or use rememberUpdatedState for latest callbacks without restart.

subtopics.title: Scroll, Focus & Key Input
subtopics.description: Use verticalScroll for small eager content, lazy containers for large lists, focus APIs for input navigation, and onPreviewKeyEvent only when early interception is required.

callouts.title: Request Focus from an Effect or Event
callouts.text: Do not call requestFocus directly during composition. Trigger it from LaunchedEffect or a user callback after the node is attached.

sections.title: Semantics, Accessibility & Testing
sections.description: Semantics describe meaning and actions to accessibility services and test tooling.

subtopics.title: Labels, Roles, State & Actions
subtopics.description: Expose what the element is, its current state, and available actions; avoid restating visible child content unnecessarily.

callouts.title: Use Built-In Semantics First
callouts.text: Material components and interaction modifiers already expose roles/actions. Add custom semantics to fill gaps, not to duplicate or conflict with built-in meaning.

subtopics.title: mergeDescendants & clearAndSetSemantics
subtopics.description: Merge related child information into one focus target; clear and replace semantics only when the default tree is misleading.

callouts.title: Inspect the Tree
callouts.text: Use the Layout Inspector or test printToLog to compare merged and unmerged semantics. Clearing semantics can accidentally remove actions and accessibility information.

subtopics.title: testTag & Stable Selectors
subtopics.description: Prefer user-visible semantics in tests. Use testTag when nodes cannot be selected reliably by accessible properties.

callouts.title: Tags Are an API
callouts.text: Tests depend on tag values, so centralize or name them semantically. Avoid tagging every node or encoding layout structure in tags.

sections.title: Parent Data, Reuse & Performance
sections.description: Some modifiers are meaningful only to a particular parent; reuse long stable chains when profiling justifies it.

subtopics.title: weight, align & matchParentSize
subtopics.description: Scoped modifiers write parent data consumed by a specific layout. Their availability signals the required receiver scope.

callouts.title: Parent Data Is Not General Styling
callouts.text: A scoped modifier outside its intended parent cannot express the same contract. Keep it near the parent-child layout relationship.

subtopics.title: Extract & Reuse Modifier Chains
subtopics.description: Modifiers are immutable and safe to reuse. Hoisting long unscoped chains can reduce allocation and comparison work in frequently recomposed UI.

callouts.title: Do Not Prematurely Globalize
callouts.text: Extract for clarity or measured hot paths. Theme-dependent, stateful, or scoped modifiers may belong inside the relevant composable/scope.

sections.title: Custom Modifiers & Debugging
sections.description: Start by composing existing modifiers; use Modifier.Node for reusable lower-level behavior.

subtopics.title: Modifier Factory Functions
subtopics.description: An extension factory preserves fluent chaining. Always include this in the returned chain.

codeBlocks.code:
fun Modifier.cardSurface(
    shape: Shape,
    color: Color
): Modifier = this
    .clip(shape)
    .background(color)
    .border(1.dp, color.copy(alpha = 0.12f), shape)

callouts.title: Do Not Break the Chain
callouts.text: Returning Modifier.background(...) instead of this.background(...) silently removes every modifier the caller supplied before the factory.

subtopics.title: Modifier.Node for Advanced Behavior
subtopics.description: Use a ModifierNodeElement plus a focused node interface such as DrawModifierNode, LayoutModifierNode, or PointerInputModifierNode when existing factories cannot express reusable behavior efficiently.

callouts.title: Update Every Mutable Parameter
callouts.text: The element update method must transfer changed parameters into the reused node and invalidate the relevant phase when required. Missing updates create stale behavior.

subtopics.title: Debugging & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Trace constraints, phase participation, order, scope, identity, and semantics.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Public composables accept modifier: Modifier = Modifier
□ Received modifier is applied to the first emitted node
□ Chain order matches hit, clip, draw, and padding intent
□ size/fill requests are compatible with parent constraints
□ offset is not mistaken for layout spacing
□ Lazy/container axes are not accidentally unbounded
□ Parent-data modifiers are in the correct scope
□ Custom factories preserve this
□ Node update propagates every changed parameter
□ Gestures use high-level semantic modifiers when possible
□ Focus is requested from an effect/event
□ Semantics are useful in merged and unmerged trees
□ Layers, intrinsics, and custom drawing are measured

callouts.title: Inspect One Wrapper at a Time
callouts.text: Temporarily add colored backgrounds/borders at different chain positions and inspect layout bounds and semantics. Most modifier bugs become obvious when the nested wrappers are visible.
